commits.message:
fix(color): ansi is measured on its table's nominal colours; ensureDrawn checks its floor at every depth

- One table per depth (DRAWN_FROM): ANSI's sixteen nominal colours stand in
  for the theme's, so ensureContrast holds the floor on them (a truecolor
  answer on another-but-unreadable index no longer passes) and ensureDrawn's
  floor holds at ansi too. The separate index-only arm is gone.
- ensureDrawn runs accept at every depth; truecolor draws from no table, so
  a refusal there is undefined like any exhausted search.
- drawnColour(colour, drawnAt, substrate?) exports the one rounding
  ensureDrawn hands its predicate.
- The seam knows a theme slot by its number, whatever depth spells it.
- One rgbDistance for every table scan.

fix(color): an ansi replacement reads against its ground's nominal colour

Text landing on its background's index was replaced by the nearest other
index, which is as often the ground's own lightness in another hue: of 1602
random collisions at a 4.5 floor, 458 drew below 2:1 against the nominal
table. It is now the nearest entry clearing the floor against the ground's
nominal colour (matchReadable), the most-contrast entry when none does: 0.
docs(contrast): ensureDrawn example declares what it measures against; states the opaque return

fix(color): screen renders at the depth it encodes; matchWhere nearest-first; ensureDrawn returns the colour it measured

- Screen passes its colorSystem in RenderOptions, so the powerline seam
  decides on the colours the frame is encoded at.
- ColorTable.matchWhere offers entries nearest-first and stops at the first
  accepted, so an expensive predicate runs only as far as the answer.
- ensureDrawn returns chosen composited opaque over its substrate — the
  colour the floor was measured on — at every depth.
- ColorSpec.fixedValue refuses an EIGHT_BIT spec on a theme slot (0-15).
- toSgrCodes' JSDoc back on toSgrCodes; strip.md states the arrow is L.bg as drawn.

fix(strip): an arrow is drawn in its left ground as drawn, and measured as the writer draws it

Style.drawnColors is the one account of the colours a style puts on screen;
toSgrCodes encodes exactly those, and the joiner measures its arrow through
them, so a translucent ground is not composited a second time over the
ground the arrow enters.

feat(color): floors hold on the colours drawn — the strip's seam, ansi text, and ensureDrawn

- RenderOptions.colorSystem: the depth the output is encoded at, set by
  renderToString and Console, so a renderable can measure what it draws
- PowerlineJoiner decides arrow or divider on the drawn colours: two grounds
  256 colours or ANSI draw as one are one ground, and the divider sits on the
  left item's own ground, so it reads exactly as that item's text
- ensureContrast at ANSI: text never lands on its background's index
- ensureDrawn(chosen, drawnAt, accept): the nearest drawable colour a stated
  floor accepts, for floors that are not text on a background
- ColorSpec.fixedValue, ColorTable.matchWhere

fix(color): contrast is chosen against a translucent background as drawn (#156)

* fix(color): contrast is chosen against a translucent background as the writer draws it

* chore(release): 0.13.1

* test(color): the truecolor path is pinned on a background translucency visibly changes

* fix(color): the surface a translucent background composites over is the caller's — black for the terminal writer, the canvas for an export

* fix(color): one SURFACE_BLACK beside compositeOver; docs say what flattens; translucent text over translucent ground pinned; 0.14.0

* fix(color): a translucent substrate is refused; docs name the drawn ground and no export wiring
